correctness.rationale: The parity-block diagonalization gives the exact Wootters concurrence including normalization. For R<J the positive limiting derivative Jt/E³ dominates a uniform O(t poly(β)e^{-β(J-R)}) derivative remainder. For R≥J a trial point below the crossing achieves J/s in the limit, compactness localizes every maximizer and excludes β(E−t) bounded, then an interior logarithmic stationarity equation yields e^{β(E−t)}~2βs and both asymptotic coefficients. The critical R=J case and squared staggered field follow directly. An independent four-dimensional Gibbs checker passed 273 seeded direct-formula and finite-optimization assertions; sampling alone is not used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Exact XX Gibbs concurrence and existence of the product–entangled crossing are known. The assessed nontrivial claim is the low-temperature global extremum on B²+b²=R², with a sharp R/J threshold, logarithmic optimizer shift and the first concurrence correction. The three accessible relevant original manuscripts develop field-dependent thermal entanglement and unconstrained local Hamiltonian tuning, but not these constrained implications. The 2003 closest article was available only as an abstract; full-text priority is a disclosed residual risk.

value.rationale: A fixed positive quadratic field norm is a physically motivated actuator budget forbidding simply turning all local fields off. The theorem gives a complete sharp budget split R<J versus R≥J, a nontrivial logarithmic thermal boundary layer, and a critical square-root staggered field at R=J. The exact leading and first-correction laws reveal why the optimized low-T entanglement differs from evaluating directly at the degenerate homogeneous field; these are meaningful structural control predictions, not a relabeling of a known concurrence formula.
